stem: Why is consistency of the light and dark schedule important in a photoperiod-sensitive flowering crop?
choices: Flowering development responds to photoperiodic signaling, so irregular light exposure can alter the intended developmental cue
Daily light integral can vary with schedule changes, so flowering is controlled primarily by the amount of electrical energy used each day
Dark-period consistency matters mainly because it standardizes room temperature, while flowering development is driven by light intensity
Keeping the same schedule improves recordkeeping and labor planning, but developmental signaling is largely independent of light-dark timing
rationale: Photoperiod-sensitive crops use light-dark timing as a developmental signal. Consistent schedules reduce unintended variation in that cue.
